shorts.title: What you will learn: Reading input with cin
shorts.hook: Make your program ask a question and listen.
shorts.script: Make your program ask a question and listen. Today your program learns to listen. It asks a question, waits, and then uses your answer. Cout sends data out to the screen. Cin brings data in from the keyboard. The arrows show the direction of the data. For cout, the arrows point toward cout. For cin, they point toward the variable. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Reading input with cin.

shorts.title: Reading input with cin in one minute
shorts.hook: Cout sends data out to the screen.
shorts.script: Cout sends data out to the screen. Cin brings data in from the keyboard. The arrows show the direction of the data. For cout, the arrows point toward cout. For cin, they point toward the variable. Think of a ticket counter. The clerk asks where you go, and you answer. First we make an int called age. Then we print a question. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: READING INPUT WITH CIN IN ONE MINUTE
shorts.caption: Reading input with cin in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: We make two ints in one line.
shorts.script: We make two ints in one line. One cin line reads both numbers. Type them with a space between. The first number goes into a. The second number goes into b. Then we print the sum, which is thirteen. Type four, a space, and nine. Then press Enter. The program prints the sum. Cout sends data out, and cin brings data in. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: The arrows point the wrong way
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. Here cin has arrows that point at cin. The compiler says no match for operator, with a long list. Do not panic. The first line is the clue. Cin needs arrows that point at the variable. Change them, and the program builds. The arrows for cin point right, toward the variable. The arrows for cout point left, toward the stream. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: THE ARROWS POINT THE WRONG WAY
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: The arrows point the wrong way.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Why did the program wait for the user? It had a lot of input about commitment.
shorts.script: Why did the program wait for the user? It had a lot of input about commitment. Ask the user for the length and width of a room. Print the area. Write your answer in the comments. Cout sends data out, and cin brings data in. The arrows point in the direction of the data. Cin stores the typed value in a variable. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
